name: Goodluck India Ltd
title: Goodluck India Ltd - 530655 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Goodluck India Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose ~38% YoY to INR13.7 bn, with EBITDA up 31% and margin pressured ~150 bps by freight and gas costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 total income grew about 38% YoY to INR13.7 bn, EBITDA rose to INR1.27 bn (9.3% margin vs 9.18%), and PAT reached INR506 mn (up ~19%). Sales volume grew 18.1% to 133,374 tonnes, while H1 volume grew 13.5% to 256,093 tonnes. Management attributed the margin squeeze to higher international freight and gas prices, estimated at ~150 bps. Management also proposed amalgamating Goodluck Defence and Aerospace and Goodluck Green Energy into Goodluck India, targeting 12–16 months for completion.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Contributes ~78% of EBITDA on ~68% of volume; EBITDA margin normally 11–13% (includes precision tubes).

segments.name: Non-value-added (normal tubes and pipes)
segments.commentary: Contributes ~22% of EBITDA on ~32% of volume; EBITDA margin normally 3–4%.

segments.name: Non-defence business
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation at 98–99% in the current quarter; debottlenecking is the main capacity lever, with capacity moving from 5 lakh to 6 lakh over 12–18 months.

segments.name: Defence (155mm shells, GDAL)
segments.commentary: No defence revenue recognised in Q2; management reiterated INR300 crore FY27 target, with revenue expected in the later part of the year. Capacity expanding from 1.5 lakh to 4 lakh shells, with peak revenue of INR1,000 crore+ at 30–35% EBITDA margin cited for the augmented capacity.

segments.name: Hydraulic tube plant
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation moved to 65–70%, with management expecting 75–80% in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin expected within 10–12%; standalone margin expected at 9–10%.
Volume and revenue growth guided at 15–20% YoY directionally for H2 FY27 and FY28.
Defence FY27 target of INR300 crore reiterated; management said it is confident of achieving it.
Non-defence capacity to rise from 5 lakh to 6 lakh tonnes in 12–18 months; defence capacity to reach 4 lakh shells in roughly 2–3 years.
Aerospace components line: ~INR80 crore investment targeted to generate ~INR180 crore business in 4–5 years.
Debt target: consolidated debt within 2.5x EBITDA; company said it is close to that level.
capex_capacity: Defence capacity expansion from 1.5 lakh to 4 lakh 155mm shells; management said it is on track and has already started, with completion guided for next financial year (2–3 years per the guideline).
Defence capital investment described as INR300 crore plus.
Transmission line capacity expansion planned within the next ~6 months.
Front fork tube expansion nearly complete, with results expected in Q4 FY27; galvanising conduit expansion under erection.
Hydraulic tube plant utilisation 65–70%; any further 50,000-tonne capex to be decided after H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Defence inquiries and LOIs exceed capacity, with management saying demand is up to three years ahead; most demand is export-driven.
GDAL is sole technically qualified bidder for 155mm HE M1A4 ready-to-fill shells for Munitions India Ltd; order not yet received and under government approval.
Defence realisations expected to stay in a 30–35% EBITDA margin band, per management.
Hydraulic tube demand improving, with utilisation rising to 65–70%.
Exports grew ~38% YoY in H1 FY27 and contributed ~28% of volumes.
Freight and fuel (gas) cost increases cut margins by ~150 bps in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR300 crore defence revenue still achievable for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated it is still hopeful and assured of maintaining the INR300 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for merger of Goodluck Defence and Goodluck India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 12–16 months (about 15 months), with SEBI and NCLT approvals required; two Big Four firms appointed for valuation, and share ratio not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Peak revenue potential from expanded defence capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak revenue of INR1,000 crore+ at 30–35% EBITDA margin, targeted by about FY29; management noted ramp-up will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Is defence revenue lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not lumpy by design but timing depends on validation, inspections and government approvals that management does not control, so yearly targets are the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debt reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle improved by about 7 days from the March 2026 exit level; debt kept within 2.5x EBITDA, with longer-term reduction planned without a specific date.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated vs standalone FY27 margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated 10–12% as guided in Q1; standalone 9–10%.

risks_watch: Freight and gas cost inflation, which cut Q2 margin by ~150 bps.
Defence revenue timing depends on government validation, inspections, geopolitical export approvals and the Munitions India order (not yet received).
Consolidated debt above INR1,000 crore, with leverage targeted within 2.5x EBITDA.
Non-defence capacity utilisation at 98–99%, which could constrain volume growth until the 6 lakh tonne expansion is complete.
Amalgamation share exchange ratio and valuation still pending; Astra development at an early stage with no licence yet.
Management did not give a specific date for net-debt-free status or for the 4 lakh shell capacity.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and defence targets, but noticeably evasive on specifics: the ratio, Astra licence, Munitions India order, and debt-reduction timing were left open. Management repeatedly stressed that defence timing rests on government approvals beyond its control.
key_quotes: So order book is not an issue. The only issue is the execution because, this particular industry, it is connected with validation, continuous inspections, and government clearances.
The volume growth we are expecting in the range of 15% to 20%.
The defence business, I will not call it a lumpy way. It is a business of the same nature.
So this realization we have maintained since beginning that it will be EBITDA margin of 30 % to 35%, and our quarter -on-quarter, we are showing it is more.

adds.what: Non-defence debottlenecking, 5 lakh to 6 lakh tonnes
Defence 155mm shell capacity expansion, 1.5 lakh to 4 lakh shells
Front fork tube expansion (nearly complete, results expected Q4 FY27)
Aerospace components line, ~INR80 cr investment for ~INR180 cr business in 4-5 years

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% and H2 FY27-FY28 volume growth of 15-20%, backed by non-defence debottlenecking (5 to 6 lakh tonnes in 12-18 months), defence capacity expansion (1.5 to 4 lakh shells, INR300 cr capex) and exports up ~38%, while non-defence utilisation is already 98-99%; defence order is not yet received (under government approval), so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 10-12% (H1 at 10.0%), but Q2 margin was squeezed ~150 bps by freight and gas costs, so recovery depends on cost normalisation and defence mix at 30-35% margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: next 6 months; 6 lakh t in 12-18 months
rows.why: Non-defence utilisation at 98-99% with debottlenecking from 5 to 6 lakh tonnes over 12-18 months, defence shell capacity expansion from 1.5 to 4 lakh already started, and transmission line expansion planned within ~6 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 15-20% consolidated volume growth for H2 FY27 and FY28; H1 volume grew 13.5% to 256,093 t and exports rose ~38%, though non-defence capacity at 98-99% limits near-term upside until the 6 lakh t expansion lands.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Hydraulic tube utilisation at 65-70% (expected 75-80% in H2 FY27) with a further 50,000 t capex to be decided after H2 FY27; non-defence utilisation at 98-99% and new transmission and galvanising lines are already in motion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue growth guidance held at 15-20% and consolidated margin at 10-12%; no sign of a raise, with H1 revenue up 34% but freight and gas headwinds ongoing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight and gas costs cut Q2 margin ~150 bps, defence INR300 cr FY27 target depends on Munitions India order (not yet received) and government approvals, and non-defence capacity is capped at 98-99% utilisation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Front fork tube expansion results expected Q4 FY27, and aerospace components line (~INR80 cr investment) targeting ~INR180 cr business in 4-5 years; Astra has no licence yet.

rows.label: Munitions India 155mm HE M1A4 order (GDAL sole qualified bidder)
rows.why: GDAL is sole technically qualified bidder but the order is not yet received and is under government approval, which gates the INR300 cr FY27 defence target.

rows.label: Amalgamation of Goodluck Defence and Goodluck Green Energy into Goodluck India
rows.why: Proposed with SEBI and NCLT approvals required and valuation by two Big Four firms; share exchange ratio not yet disclosed.

rows.label: Consolidated debt within 2.5x EBITDA
rows.why: Management says it is close to 2.5x EBITDA now with H1 EBITDA at INR2.67 bn, and longer-term reduction is planned but without a specific date.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15-20% growth outlook, the INR300 cr defence target and the 1,000 cr+ peak revenue potential, but was evasive on the share ratio, Munitions India order timing, Astra licence and debt-reduction dates; analysts pressed on defence lumpiness and margin recovery.
